claims.statement: agent/dashboard/options.py is the single registry of selectable models: SUPPORTED_MODELS is a hand-maintained list of ModelOption records (provider-prefixed id, label, per-model efforts list, default_effort, supports_images), and SUPPORTED_MODEL_IDS is the frozen set every resolution layer checks membership against.

The efforts a model accepts are per-model and non-uniform (for example Kimi K3 only accepts low/high/max and Gemini uses minimal through high), and model_supports_effort/model_supports_images validate a stored selection against the model's own ModelOption fields.

Deprecated model ids are not canonically replaced: DEPRECATED_MODEL_REPLACEMENTS has empty values and canonical_model_pair always returns None. Deprecated ids are excluded from provider_fallback_pair and defer to defaults, while unsupported non-deprecated ids may use same-provider and, where possible, same-Claude-family fallback.

default_model_pair() is the deployment-level terminal fallback: it reads LLM_MODEL_ID and LLM_REASONING_EFFORT, validates that the resulting model is supported and default-eligible, and raises ValueError for an unsupported model or effort.

For a hosted agent run, the factory seeds workspace main/subagent defaults, applies a profile only when no stored thread model exists, then uses stored thread settings when present; a valid explicit configurable agent_model_id/agent_effort replaces that snapshot and the resolved settings are persisted back to the thread.

agent_overrides.resolve_agent_model_id resolves a supported per-thread id over a valid profile override over the effective workspace default; deprecated or unsupported per-thread ids do not replace that lower-precedence result.

Every workspace-default resolution routes candidates through _resolve_default_pair, which returns the pair if supported, else the same-provider fallback, else the global default, guaranteeing a valid constructible pair when the store is stale or a selection is unknown.

Instance defaults are stored as the LangGraph Store record keyed 'default' in the ['team_settings'] namespace, while workspace overrides use ['workspace_settings']; get_workspace_settings overlays hardcoded, instance, and workspace values and degrades to hardcoded defaults on store failure.

WorkspaceSettings resolves distinct defaults per role (agent/reviewer/chat), where chat inherits the workspace agent default when no chat-specific model is configured; it also has separate subagent, adaptive-routing tier, and thread-title resolvers.

Per-user profiles live in the ['profiles'] namespace holding default model and effort, an optional subagent pair, repository/branch and PR preferences, and routing preferences; profile-editable settings are deliberately split from encrypted GitHub OAuth tokens in ['oauth_tokens'] so a profile save and a concurrent login/refresh cannot clobber each other's fields.

On the run-start path profiles are read fail-soft (agent_overrides.load_profile logs and returns None so a store blip costs only per-user overrides), whereas dashboard reads use profiles.get_profile so failures surface.

normalize_profile_overrides accepts a profile's default_model and reasoning_effort only when both are valid and default-eligible, otherwise falls back to the same-provider pair for an unsupported id, and returns (None, None) for an absent or unknown-provider selection so the workspace default applies.

provider_model_kwargs translates a resolved effort string into provider-specific kwargs by dispatching on the model id prefix: OpenAI gets a reasoning dict (summary auto for non-none efforts), Anthropic gets adaptive/summarized thinking plus an effort field, Gemini 3+ gets thinking_level, Fireworks gets model_kwargs.reasoning_effort, and Baseten gets reasoning_effort for low/high/max.

make_model builds a chat model via init_chat_model and applies a default max_retries of 6 and a 600-second per-request timeout for known provider prefixes so a stalled provider connection becomes a retry instead of a wedged run.

make_model configures OpenAI models for the Responses API with store=false, output_version responses/v1, and include reasoning.encrypted_content, and uses desktop OpenAI OAuth when no OPENAI_API_KEY is set and the gateway is not applied.
make_model routes Baseten as an OpenAI-compatible provider and, when the gateway is disabled, requires BASETEN_API_KEY and points at the Baseten base URL, raising if the key is missing.

Gateway routing is tri-state: resolve_gateway_enabled treats a workspace gateway_enabled of True/False as authoritative and None as inheriting the LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_ENABLED deployment default (or a dedicated gateway-key default), and when enabled gateway_overrides supplies base_url/api_key/use_responses_api that override direct-provider defaults.

fallback_model_id_for returns a cross-provider fallback (Anthropic primaries to OpenAI and vice versa) and None for Google, local, or self-hosted providers that must not be silently re-routed; the run factory wires this into ModelFallbackMiddleware honoring an LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID env override first.

Fable models are gated workspace-wide: disabling Fable rewrites Fable workspace defaults to a safe non-Fable Anthropic pair, and the factory gates main, subagent, and title models after resolution so disabled Fable is not constructed from a stale snapshot.

Per-repo custom instructions are access-controlled records stored in the ['agent_instructions'] namespace keyed by owner/name; for a new thread the factory resolves them for the effective repository, stores them in the thread snapshot, and renders them into the shared system prompt.

Per-user custom instructions live in their own ['user_instructions'] namespace keyed by GitHub login and capped at 20,000 characters because both the dashboard and the agent's save_user_instructions tool write them, preventing profile-save and agent-tool writers from clobbering each other.

During preparation the factory loads each participant's current personal instructions into dynamic person context; the collaboration prompt scopes standing instructions to acting on that person's request and makes repository instructions and AGENTS.md authoritative on conflict.

Instruction conflicts resolve with AGENTS.md over repository custom instructions, repository custom instructions over workspace instructions, and repository/AGENTS guidance over personal standing instructions.

Thread settings are a cached agent_settings metadata snapshot containing typed model, routing, and repository-instruction fields; malformed data normalizes to an empty snapshot and failed reads or writes are logged without aborting a run.

Adaptive model routing uses a profile preference over a workspace opt-in default and then freezes the thread setting; when enabled ModelSelectionMiddleware persists a fast, balanced, or performance route, classifies only in auto mode, and falls back to balanced on classifier failure.

Workspace instructions are rendered into the system prompt separately from repository custom instructions, while construct_system_prompt loads configured default instructions from DEFAULT_PROMPT_PATH or the bundled default prompt.
